forces.title: Shrinking European natural gas demand by 2% annually.
forces.description: European natural gas demand is projected to decline by an average of 2 percent per year until 2030. This structural shift is primarily driven by the accelerated electrification of transport, buildings (heat pumps), data centers, and industry. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this means reduced throughput volumes, which can negatively impact tariff-regulated revenues and the utilization of existing network assets, necessitating strategic adaptation.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

forces.title: EU's Heating and Cooling Strategy reduces natural gas reliance.
forces.description: The European Commission's 2026 Heating and Cooling Strategy aims to reduce reliance on natural gas in the heating and cooling sector, which currently accounts for half of EU energy consumption and is 70% fossil fuel-dependent. This strategy promotes integrated local heat planning, district heating modernization, and renewable heat sources. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this represents a significant headwind by driving a structural shift away from natural gas for end-use heating applications.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

forces.title: Continued capital allocation to regulated gas network assets by utilities.
forces.description: Selected European utilities are allocating substantial capital to regulated network assets, including gas infrastructure. Exhibit 7 shows investments in total networks' Regulatory Asset Base (RAB), encompassing both electricity and gas networks. This trend signifies ongoing commitment to maintaining and potentially upgrading gas distribution networks, providing a measure of stability and predictable returns for Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities through regulated asset base frameworks, despite broader demand shifts.
forces.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

forces.title: Geopolitical disruptions threaten India's natural gas supply chain stability.
forces.description: India's significant dependence on West Asian energy corridors, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, exposes its natural gas supply chain to severe disruptions from geopolitical conflicts. Any re-closure of the Strait immediately squeezes supply, potentially leading to domestic inflation and impacting the profitability of downstream sectors that rely on gas. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this risk translates to potential supply shortages for their networks, affecting reliability of service and potentially impacting regulated revenue streams.

forces.title: India's policy aims to reduce imported gas, promoting alternative energy sources.
forces.description: India is strategically committed to reducing its reliance on imported oil and gas by focusing on developing alternative domestic energy sources such as syngas from coal gasification and nuclear energy. This initiative aims to insulate the economy from persistent external energy shocks. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this represents a long-term structural shift in the energy mix, potentially altering the availability and pricing of gas commodity inputs into the city gate, and influencing future network expansion strategies.

forces.title: LNG supply disruptions cause distribution delays for commercial users.
forces.description: Disruptions in LNG flows, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions in West Asia, have led to distribution delays for commercial gas users in India. These delays result from surging domestic LNG prices and strained reserves due to reliance on imports. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this poses a key operational risk, as interrupted supply directly affects their ability to deliver gas to commercial end-customers, potentially impacting service quality, regulated revenue targets, and customer satisfaction.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: CGD sector's high reliance on RLNG imports for consumption.
forces.description: The City Gas Distribution (CGD) sector in India has one of the highest consumptions of Regasified Liquefied Natural Gas (RLNG) among various sectors. This indicates a structural dependence on imported gas for a significant portion of its supply requirements. While this ensures a base demand for distribution, it also inherently exposes the IN100201 sector to global LNG price volatility and supply chain vulnerabilities, making it sensitive to international energy market dynamics.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Integration of upgraded biomethane into city gas distribution networks.
forces.description: A key policy recommendation is to integrate upgraded biomethane (Bio-CNG) into city gas distribution (CGD) networks. Biomethane, produced from locally available biomass, offers a domestic alternative feedstock for natural gas, reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels. This initiative serves as a significant upside driver for Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, enabling greater energy sovereignty, supply stability, and potentially lower input costs while aligning with broader decarbonization goals.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: India's green transition strategy maintains natural gas investment.
forces.description: India's strategy for a green energy transition, focused on energy availability, affordability, and sustainability, includes continued investment in natural gas, LNG, and hydrogen. This implies natural gas will serve as a crucial transitional fuel to support decarbonization while meeting rising energy needs over the next two decades. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this is a significant tailwind, ensuring sustained demand for gas distribution services and potentially supporting network expansion.

viewpoints.title: European gas utilities must diversify into power as demand shrinks post-2030.
viewpoints.description: McKinsey anticipates European natural gas demand to decline by 2% annually until 2030, emphasizing the necessity for historical gas utilities to expand into power value chain activities. This suggests a cautious outlook for traditional gas utilities that do not strategically diversify, as their core business faces structural demand reduction, driving a strategic evolution within the sector towards integrated models to manage risk and maintain value creation.
viewpoints.source_title: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead

viewpoints.title: India's gas supply chain vulnerable to geopolitical shocks, necessitates energy diversification.
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings states India remains vulnerable to natural gas supply chain disruptions, particularly from the Strait of Hormuz, despite diversifying crude oil sources. This vulnerability squeezes supply, potentially triggering domestic inflation and compressing profit margins across downstream sectors. CareEdge emphasizes the need to reduce imported oil and gas share and develop alternative sources like syngas and nuclear energy to build resilience, indicating a cautious view on the stability of gas supply for distributors.

viewpoints.title: India's LNG dependence creates structural energy shocks, impacting domestic gas distribution.
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights India's significant reliance on imported LNG (approx. 50% of demand, concentrated in the Gulf) makes its energy system structurally vulnerable to external shocks, as demonstrated by Strait of Hormuz disruptions. These disruptions cause domestic LNG price surges, strain reserves, and lead to distribution delays, specifically for commercial users. KPMG identifies this as impacting the entire supply chain, implicitly affecting Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities responsible for last-mile distribution to end consumers.
viewpoints.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

viewpoints.title: Integrating biomethane with CGD networks crucial for India's gas sector resilience.
viewpoints.description: KPMG recommends integrating upgraded biomethane with city gas distribution (CGD) networks as a key policy measure to build domestic resilience in India's energy strategy. This approach aims to diversify feedstock sources, reducing dependence on imported hydrocarbons and mitigating geopolitical risks. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this signifies a positive future pathway, enabling more stable and localized supply inputs while enhancing overall energy security and reliability of their networks and services.
viewpoints.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

viewpoints.title: India's energy transition strategy supports natural gas investment for decarbonization.
viewpoints.description: IBEF highlights that India's green energy transition plan, aimed at balancing energy availability, affordability, and sustainability, involves investing in natural gas, LNG, and hydrogen. This strategy positions natural gas as a crucial element to support decarbonization efforts while simultaneously meeting the nation's growing energy demands over the next two decades. For Gas Transmission & Distribution Utilities, this indicates a positive outlook, ensuring continued relevance and demand for their services as gas acts as a transitional fuel in India's evolving energy mix.

demand_drivers.description: Increased adoption of electric vehicles and residential heat pumps reduces reliance on natural gas for energy consumption.
Electrified industrial processes decrease industrial demand for natural gas.
Policy shifts and targets for renewable energy drive reduced fossil fuel consumption across sectors.

pnl_drivers.description: Lower natural gas demand leads to reduced volumes transported and distributed, potentially impacting tariff-regulated revenue for gas utilities.
